chapter: Advice to youth and the art of drumming
title: Today's drummers lack the old beat and bass drum
summary: Saunders says many young drummers fool with the left hand and play tricks with the bass drum instead of giving a back beat and bottom.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: That's right. Now, you can learn a lot of things about playing jazz, in schools and -- but drummers particularly -- how do you learn what a beat is?
Yeah, you can't, you don't learn.

Right, right, you've got -- no, no, no, right, that's right. And this is what I find that's lacking so much in most of the drummers that you run across today. They don't have that drive and that beat that you're talking about. They just don't have it. They're fooling
around with that left hand so much. And they don't give you that old back beat and that old sound that you want.
And the bass drum is another thing. They're playing tricks with it. Their feet are dancing, and they're trying to see how many taps they can make with it.
It's nothing like, say, a four-piece rhythm section in a big band, and the drummer playing the bass drum --
Get that round sound, lift the band up.
Sure. If it's not there, then you listen and you fill this emptiness.
